# Workspace ONE AutoPkg recipes

This skill is self-contained. It uses ordinary file/shell tools, not a particular coding-harness SDK. Resolve every resource path relative to this SKILL.md, not the shell working directory. Read referenced files explicitly; do not assume automatic loading or host-specific slash commands.

## Before changing files

1. Read the target checkout's AGENTS.md and neighboring recipes. Confirm which recipe types are requested and whether existing files may be changed.
2. Discover AutoPkg, its version, the selected Python interpreter, and available format/lint tools. Do not pin an unrelated project's runtime or silently install/upgrade software.
3. Search existing community recipes and inspect actual parent files, including shared processors. Prefer a maintained Munki parent and preserve its metadata/scripts. A sibling pkg recipe's outputs are not inherited through a shared download parent.
4. Read [references/parents-and-validation.md](references/parents-and-validation.md) before choosing overrides, version logic, or validation commands. For new download/pkg/Munki parent creation, the published [homebysix recipe-creation skill](https://github.com/autopkg/homebysix-recipes/blob/master/.claude/skills/create-autopkg-recipes/SKILL.md) is useful optional guidance. It is not a required local companion; adapt its repository-specific conventions rather than importing them wholesale.

## Names and layout

- Reusable recipes belong in `ws1-recipes/`; custom parents belong in `ws1-parent-recipes/`. Do not edit shared processors just to scaffold an application.
- Separate the compact file/identifier suffix (`ExampleApp`) from Input.NAME (`Vendor Example App`). Use the vendor's marketing name with a vendor prefix if not already present, preserving spaces. Record the source in review notes. Do not disrupt existing recipe names by silently renaming them.
- Set the same NAME in importer, assigner, and pruner. Hub uses the app name rather than relying on Munki's display_name. Confirm the parent's `pkginfo.name` uses `%NAME%`, and inspect other NAME-dependent paths. If the name is hard-coded, override intentionally without discarding other metadata.
- Inherit pkginfo by default. Do not invent a minimum OS, architecture, category, catalog policy, or installer script just to fill a template.
- In a separate CI/CD checkout, use its workflow-defined root, overrides, repo/cache directories, exported preferences, reports, and recipe lists. Do not substitute home-directory defaults. The public [AutoPkg-WS1-example](https://github.com/equinor/AutoPkg-WS1-example) is one example, not a universal layout. Deployment-project setup belongs in that project's instructions, not in generic recipe defaults.

## Generate scaffolds

Generation requires Python 3.9+ and PyYAML. Use an existing suitable interpreter or ask before installing dependencies. From this skill directory:

```sh
python3 scripts/new_ws1_recipe.py ExampleApp \
  --name 'Vendor Example App' \
  --identifier-prefix com.github.codeskipper \
  --parent 'com.github.vendor.munki.ExampleApp' \
  --out /path/to/checkout/ws1-recipes
```

The parent above is illustrative, not an existing recipe claim. All three types are generated by default; `--only importer`, `--only assigner`, or `--only pruner` supports staged work. The generator never runs AutoPkg or overwrites files. Existing NAME/identifier/parent conflicts must be reviewed, not silently mixed into the set.

The recipe namespace is separate from the shared processor namespace. Processors default to `com.github.codeskipper.OMNISSA-WorkSpaceOne{Importer,Assigner,Pruner}`. Change `--processor-prefix` only for a verified processor fork.

Templates use `.recipe.yaml.in` to avoid being mistaken for runnable recipes. Generated files use `.recipe.yaml`. They are scaffolds with placeholder credentials/assignment/retention inputs, not ready-to-run deployment policies.

## Configuration and safeguards

- Auth Input keys are uppercase `WS1_*`; processor Arguments are lowercase `ws1_*` with string substitutions. Never put real secrets, tenants, organization IDs, or smart groups in published templates.
- Complex inputs such as `ws1_app_assignments` must be lowercase Input lists/dicts consumed directly, not `%VAR%` strings. For AppsV2 assignments, clear the simple smart-group input; do not supply both methods. Preserve `#AUTOPKG` / `#AUTOPKG_DONE` behavior.
- Retention and safeguard options expected as strings must stay strings. The safeguard's `"1"` means enabled for this processor; do not assume another option interprets numeric strings the same way.
- Pruner scaffolds explicitly select `dry_run`. Dry runs still authenticate/query UEM and require permission. Change deletion mode only with explicit approval. Retention placeholders are not a safety boundary: the processor may fall back to a default.
- Keep UEM's version aligned with Munki metadata, including any necessary normalization. Do not normalize version formats without inspecting the application and target requirements.
- Preserve scripts inherited from the Munki parent unless a change is justified. Inspect how the importer passes pkginfo to UEM; do not assume scripts are ignored.

## Validate and report

1. Run `plistyamlplist <file> --tidy` if available. For plist/YAML conversion use that tool, not hand conversion. Do not silently install it. Omit unused Comment keys instead of emitting nulls; durable notes belong in Comment because YAML comments may be dropped.
2. Run `python3 scripts/lint_recipes.py --ws1 <files>`. This is limited structural lint, not processor/schema/runtime validation. Review formatting round trips for YAML scalar type changes.
3. Run the repository's existing strict recipe checks and `git diff --check`. Report tool/configuration incompatibilities; do not bypass hooks or upgrade dependencies without approval.
4. Use `autopkg info -q <recipe>` with the project's explicit `--prefs` where applicable to check resolution/merged inputs. Output can contain credentials from overrides: do not print it wholesale. Identify missing repos; ask before cloning/setup changes.
5. Review parent/shared-processor code before recording trust. Never blindly update trust following a verification failure.
6. Only with approval, test processing against a defined destination. `--check` is not a universal dry run: inspect EndOfCheckPhase placement; a chain without a check boundary may reach upload processors. Do not execute importer/assigner/pruner recipes merely to validate syntax or discovery.

Do not use AutoPkg verbosity above 2 with credentials; review/redact lower-level output too. Never print token/keychain contents or private configuration wholesale. Do not enable shell pre-approval or disable the host sandbox to make the workflow work.

Distinguish offline lint, parent resolution, download/signature tests, and live deployment results in the final report. Native macOS installer/DMG operations require suitable macOS tools; configured CAR workflows may run platform-independent assignment/pruning on Linux. A cloud editing/review session is not automatically such a deployment environment.
